headline: High: next-ai-draw-io can exfiltrate sensitive document content via broad egress and MCP, while EMQX can ingest and relay IoT data without pairwise isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: next-ai-draw-io uses MCP and browser-based document processing, so malicious content in PDFs/text can plausibly steer tool use. EMQX exposes an HTTP API and broad network egress, but no shared channel is documented, so the interaction is inferred rather than proven. Uncertainty keeps this at medium, not low.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io ingests attacker-controlled PDF/text and forwards instructions through MCP
IF EMQX output is copied into next-ai-draw-io without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable MCP tool execution for untrusted documents
Strip instructions from imported files before processing
Use a separate workspace for EMQX outputs
Add a human review step before any tool call
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data and has broad network egress; next-ai-draw-io handles PDFs, images, and API keys. If they share a workspace or operator context, document contents or IoT data can leak through the document agent's outbound model/API calls. The pairwise path is plausible but not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents access the same files or pasted content
IF next-ai-draw-io sends imported document text to a third-party model endpoint
mitigations: Keep IoT data and documents in separate folders
Remove secrets from files before opening them in next-ai-draw-io
Use local-only models for document processing
Rotate any API keys exposed to the document agent
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: EMQX has HTTP API access and next-ai-draw-io can use MCP plus multiple model backends, but neither profile shows shared write access to the same mutable resource. The main overlap is networked control surfaces, not a proven write conflict. Because no shared filesystem or lockless mutation target is documented, severity stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external resource
IF an orchestrator maps EMQX HTTP actions and next-ai-draw-io MCP actions onto one mutable backend
mitigations: Assign separate service accounts
Avoid pointing both agents at the same mutable endpoint
Serialize any shared writes manually
Check for duplicate updates after each run
requires-engineering: add resource locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: next-ai-draw-io produces AI-assisted visualizations from documents, and EMQX exposes an HTTP API that could consume or relay resulting artifacts. If EMQX treats the diagram agent's output as authoritative, errors can cascade from document interpretation into downstream actions. The profiles do not prove such automation, so this remains medium.
conditions: IF EMQX ingests next-ai-draw-io output without verification
IF a generated diagram or extracted text is used as the basis for an API action
mitigations: Require manual approval before acting on generated output
Compare outputs against source documents
Log source-to-action traceability
Limit EMQX actions to read-only during review
requires-engineering: add validation gates

E_compliance.rationale: next-ai-draw-io handles PDF/text/image content and requests API keys, while EMQX touches IoT data. If regulated or personal data is placed into the document agent, its broad egress and third-party model options can create residency or retention mismatches. EMQX has no explicit compliance controls in profile, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated IoT data or personal documents are processed by either agent
IF next-ai-draw-io routes content to non-approved external model providers
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the document agent
Use approved regional model endpoints only
Review retention settings for all providers
Redact identifiers before upload
requires-engineering: document residency and retention policy
